cand.title: Pathways to Peace: Second International Conference on Returning Ukrainian Children, Detained Civilians, and Prisoners of War
cand.organizationName: Global Affairs Canada, Ukraine and Norway
cand.excerpt: Two-day ministerial international conference in Toronto co-hosted by Canada, Ukraine and Norway, bringing foreign ministers, senior government representatives, international organisations, civil society and experts together for plenaries and thematic exchanges. This is a strong fit for executive guestrooms, secure meeting, interpretation, catering and protocol-related event demand, without evidence of hotel contracting.
cand.selectionWhy: Prior blocked-promising candidate (no exact date/contact in thin ledger)

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: No verified hotel-contracting buyer identified. Kateryna Sherysheva, Chief of Staff, Ukraine Task Force, Global Affairs Canada, is the named contact on the event-specific Canada Gazette order: strongest event-linked referral route, but her published remit is not accommodation procurement. Veronica Panton, Ontario Chief of Protocol & Director, International Relations, is a secondary, indirect delegation-planning referral; no event-specific role or purchasing authority is established. Political co-hosts Anita Anand, Denys Uliutin and Eivind Vad Petersson are not treated as hotel buyers.
findings.futureEdition: No next edition with officially published dates and city was identified for December 2026–June 2028. The September 28–29, 2026 Toronto conference is past; October 1 is the concluding release publication date, not an activity date. Continued policy work and the 2026–2027 Forward-Looking Agenda are not announcements of another conference.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specifications and the published delegation profile: a downtown city-hotel role is more plausible than a resort retreat, conditional on a future Toronto activity. Radisson Blu Toronto Downtown could pitch a limited delegation, expert or VIP room block and small bilateral/side meetings—not exclusive conference accommodation. The Gazette anticipated that privileges and immunities would cover about 400 participants; this is not verified total attendance or room demand. A 157-room hotel with an approximately 240-theatre largest room should not be positioned as the sole lodging and plenary solution for that scale. The supplied 15–109 peak-room sales band is a targeting range only, not event demand. Security, protocol, interpretation/AV, transport, room availability and food-and-beverage operations require qualification; no secure-meeting or catering capability is assumed.
findings.venueCommitments: Toronto, Ontario, Canada is verified. Exact facility and street address remain unverified. Consequently, Harbourfront/downtown/MTCC/Exhibition Place proximity cannot be established; neither a suburban venue nor a competing hotel can be asserted. No future venue commitment identified.
findings.historicalRotation: The linked predecessor was the Ministerial Conference on the Human Dimension of Ukraine’s 10-Point Peace Formula, October 30–31, 2024, Montréal, Québec, Canada. The second conference took place September 28–29, 2026, Toronto, Ontario, Canada. Exact facilities for both remain unknown. These establish two related editions in different cities, not an annual/biennial schedule, contractual rotation or guaranteed Toronto return.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Unknown. No edition-specific host hotel, official housing bureau, room block, accommodation booking link, open hotel RFP or lodging contract award was identified. Hotels listed in relevant edition-specific sources reviewed: none. This is not evidence of no bookings or of open inventory. The official announcement says only “in Toronto, Ontario, on September 28 and 29, 2026”; its media advisory addresses accreditation rather than hotel sourcing. No lodging-source quote is available because the reviewed official pages do not publish a lodging mechanism.
findings.organizationStructure: Intergovernmental ministerial conference co-hosted by Canada through Global Affairs Canada, Ukraine and Norway; not an association meeting or corporate-owned conference. No PCO, DMC, agency or housing contractor was identified. Event ownership and policy leadership do not establish which department, contractor or individual delegation contracted hotels.
findings.competitiveLimitations: No incumbent hotel or contracted housing bureau was identified; commitment elsewhere and availability are both unknown. No evidence of overflow, compression, unmet room demand or competitive displacement was found. The actual conference facility is unknown, so the hotel’s waterfront location and MTCC walkability do not establish event proximity. Individual delegations may be a sourcing route only as an explicit hypothesis, not a verified purchasing arrangement.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Remove from the active dated-event sales pipeline and retain as historical government-account development, subject to ORS qualification. First request a brief routing conversation with Kateryna Sherysheva: ask who handled hotel/accommodation procurement for 2026, whether any follow-on Toronto meeting is authorized, whether sourcing is central or delegation-led, and what supplier onboarding/security requirements apply. If appropriate, seek a protocol referral through Veronica Panton. Only after a future Toronto activity and buying route are confirmed, offer a capacity-limited delegation block and small meetings; verify restaurant/lounge/catering, AV/interpretation and security requirements before quoting. Do not solicit ministers as purchasing contacts.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: Closed as a current-edition sales opportunity: the activity concluded September 29, 2026, before the research cutoff. No live room block or RFP established. The previous SALES_READY label is unsupported by current evidence.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Conditional relationship-development hypothesis only. The 2024 predecessor and 2026 second edition support a continuing policy-convening relationship, but no next dates, host city, Toronto return or sourcing window are announced in the sources found. Do not create a future Toronto room-night forecast or call this recurring competitive capture yet.
